title: Integrate policy engine with Optimize apply endpoint (hard block on fail; soft block w/ override behind feature flag)
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Goal
- Gate Optimize “apply” behind quality guardrails: consult policy engine, surface decision in API + Console, and enforce blocking behavior with staged rollout.

Scope
- Optimize control-plane apply endpoint(s): both Console-initiated and API-initiated applies.
- Synchronous policy evaluation + async eval-run orchestration integration.
- Enforcement modes:
  1) Observe-only: run + record decision, do not block.
  2) Soft-block: fail gating returns blocked unless override is provided (override behind feature flag + RBAC; audit required).
  3) Hard-block: fail gating blocks apply unconditionally.

Non-goals
- Implementing override RBAC/approval workflow itself (tracked in ENG-3920).
- Defining thresholds/metric taxonomy (Applied ML docs + PM tickets).

Implementation outline
- Add Guardrails gating step to apply flow:
  1) Build “proposed config delta” from Optimize recommendation (batching/caching/quantization/routing knobs).
  2) Call Policy Engine: EvaluateGuardrails(tenant, route/model, model_version, prompt_set_rev, optimization_type, config_delta, enforcement_context).
  3) If evaluation requires an eval run (no cached result / stale), request Eval Runner job and return “pending/timeout” state per enforcement mode.
  4) Persist gating decision summary + eval_run_id on apply attempt for audit/debug.

API behavior
- Apply request returns a stable gating envelope with:
  - decision: PASS | FAIL | PENDING | ERROR
  - enforcement: OBSERVE_ONLY | SOFT_BLOCK | HARD_BLOCK
  - failure_reasons: metric + threshold violated + CI/sample-size notes (when FAIL)
  - eval_run_id + artifact links (if available)
  - override_required/override_accepted (if soft-block and caller provided override)

Enforcement rules (initial)
- Hard-block: FAIL => do not apply config; return 409 (or 412) with gating payload.
- Soft-block: FAIL => return 409/412 unless override token/flag is present AND caller has permission; apply proceeds but is marked override=true in audit.
- PENDING/ERROR/timeout: default to blocked for Enterprise tiers unless explicitly configured to “manual approval” (tie into safe-degrade decision; see ENG-3926/PR 18571).

Acceptance criteria
- Apply endpoint calls policy engine deterministically for same inputs.
- Observe-only mode logs decisions + emits audit event but never blocks.
- Soft-block mode blocks applies on FAIL unless override is supplied (behind feature flag).
- Hard-block mode blocks applies on FAIL even if override is supplied.
- Failure payload is actionable: includes metric deltas, threshold, CI/sample-size gating notes, and eval_run_id.
- Audit event includes gating decision + enforcement mode + override fields (see ENG-3918).

Links
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/optimize-quality-guardrails-gating-prd.json
- UX spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/optimize-apply-flow-gating-ux-spec.json
- Enforcement ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-optimize-gating-enforcement-point.json
- Policy schema work: ENG-3912
- Eval runner: ENG-3914

Notes / open questions
- Finalize HTTP status codes + error taxonomy for client UX (Console wants distinct states for FAIL vs TIMEOUT).
- Determine which tiers can ever proceed on PENDING/ERROR (default should be “block” to avoid silent regressions).
- Confirm which field(s) represent “override requested” vs “override approved” once RBAC lands.
comments: 2025-01-14 (Ethan Park): Creating ENG-3913 to track apply endpoint enforcement wiring. The policy engine decision must be the single gate for both Console and API applies. Please align response shape with Kenji’s UX spec (pass/fail/timeout states + metric deltas).

2025-01-16 (Brian Murphy): Started implementation plan. Proposal: apply endpoint always returns a `gating` object. In observe-only we still compute decision and emit audit event; apply proceeds. In soft/hard block we return 412 Precondition Failed for gating=FAIL/PENDING. Need PM signoff on status code vs 409.

2025-01-17 (Jordan Lee): Policy engine can return FAIL w/ reasons, or REQUIRE_EVAL when no cached eval summary exists. For determinism: ensure metric keys are sorted and policy evaluation uses stable rounding rules. We’ve seen non-deterministic map iteration cause flaky decisions elsewhere; please normalize ordering before hashing/caching.

2025-01-21 (Aditya Rao): Product preference: 412 for “blocked by guardrails” to distinguish from quota/permission errors; include `blocked_reason=quality_guardrails` for support tooling. Soft-block should show “Request override” CTA in Console; for API callers we’ll allow an `override=true` flag but only behind feature gate + RBAC (ENG-3920).

2025-01-24 (Brian Murphy): Implemented `guardrails_enforcement_mode` gate with 3 states: observe-only, soft-block, hard-block. Default observe-only for all tenants. Tenant-level config will be set by rollout (ENG-3926). Added internal header `X-Redwood-Guardrails-Debug` to attach eval_run_id on blocked responses for easier support triage (header only; not for public docs).

2025-01-28 (Naomi Feldman): Security review note: override attempts must be auditable even when blocked (i.e., user tried to override but lacked permission). Please ensure audit payload doesn’t include raw prompts or rubric text; only summary metrics + identifiers.

2025-02-02 (Sean Gallagher): Failure mode: if policy engine or eval runner is unavailable, we need predictable behavior. For pilot we should block applies (soft-block/hard-block) and surface a clear “Guardrails service unavailable” reason. For observe-only we should not fail the apply; just emit a degraded signal and page only if error budget is exceeded. Track safe-degrade specifics in ENG-3926 / PR 18571.

2025-02-06 (Brian Murphy): Open point: when Policy Engine returns REQUIRE_EVAL, we enqueue eval job and return PENDING. In soft-block/hard-block this blocks apply; in observe-only apply proceeds (but logs PENDING). Console will poll the gating summary endpoint (ENG-3917/PR 18496) to display final results.

2025-02-08 (Brian Murphy): PR up for core apply enforcement + response shape: sources/github/redwood/pr_18435.json. Includes unit tests for: PASS allows apply; FAIL blocks in hard-block; FAIL requires override in soft-block; observe-only never blocks. Still need integration test coverage in ENG-3924.

2025-02-11 (Selene Huang): Review feedback: make sure failure_reasons include sample-size failure separately from metric regression (we need to distinguish “insufficient evidence” vs “regressed”). Also: when quantization change is proposed, we must include suite_selector tag in request (quant-only suites are mandatory per quant policy).

2025-02-13 (Brian Murphy): Addressed Selene feedback: added explicit reason codes `INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE_SIZE`, `CI_OVERLAP`, `METRIC_REGRESSION`, `EVAL_TIMEOUT`, `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. For quantization changes, apply now passes `optimization_type=quantization_profile_transition` to policy engine (suite selector handled downstream in eval runner integration).

2025-02-18 (Ethan Park): Marking Done. Merged PR 18435. Next: override permissions/justification (ENG-3920 + PR 18518), safe-degrade behavior (PR 18571), and docs alignment once enforcement starts shifting from observe-only.
